segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [faint water movement] [softly] Sit or lie comfortably and let the first breaths be entirely ordinary. Imagine calm blue water beneath the lower ribs.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Place one hand on the upper chest and one around the belly or lower ribs, if touch feels helpful.
[soft, slow, warm voice] As air arrives, invite the lower hand to move a little. Picture a luminous jellyfish bell widening without hurry.
[soft, slow, warm voice] As air leaves, the bell gathers inward. Do not squeeze it empty; let the water complete the motion.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel expansion around the sides and back of the lower ribs as well as the front. The whole soft ring may participate.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] Keep each breath comfortable. If you feel light-headed, short of breath, or strained, return immediately to natural breathing.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Continue with an easy rhythm: widening... gathering... widening... gathering. No number needs to govern the sea.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let the shoulders remain quiet while the deeper movement does less visible work below.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice whether the breath can become smoother rather than bigger. A small jellyfish still travels perfectly well.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Release the image and feel the actual body breathing, supported by muscles that already know the route.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Take several unshaped breaths. Observe what continues by itself when you stop helping.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Let the hands rest. Return to the room with the lower ribs spacious and the breath free to choose its own tide.
